tb21_profile.skill: Reverse-engineer a compiled executable - via static inspection, dynamic tracing, or crafted interaction - to recover an embedded secret it never means to reveal, and write it out
tb21_profile.domain: Binary reverse engineering / CTF: ELF and service binaries, strings/objdump/gdb/radare2, format-string and buffer-overflow exploitation
tb21_profile.task_form: reverse-engineer-a-binary-or-protocol: probe an opaque executable until the secret falls out, then save it to a file

verifier_notes: CalibForge security_20260514_010833_001 is graded FREE in the packet but 'ok' in verifier_strength.json - I trusted the packet's FREE and excluded it entirely. notes: This TB2.1 task has unusually strong coverage. The two new corpora both beat the old ones here: CalibForge has a dedicated 'security' category of extract-a-secret-from-a-binary tasks that are near-clones of TB2.1 (hardcoded MASTERKEY{}/SECRET{}/FLAG{} in auth binaries, socket oracles, format-string leaks) with graded verifiers - six of the final ten. TerminalWorld also has genuine crackme RE (tw_383451, tw_289006) but its very best pure matches are FREE-graded. TMax contributes deep binary-RE tasks (extract hardcoded key from ELF, reverse a token checker). Terminal-Lego only offers binary-tooling exercises (disassemble/objdump/ELF structure), not secret extraction - moderate transfer at best. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has real CTF/flag tasks (Bandit suconnect, OSCP/SUID privesc, Chepy decode chains) but ALL are graded 'absent' (no verifier ships), so despite good skill match they rank below the graded CalibForge/TW/TMax equivalents. SWE-Smith/Rebench only reach binary-format-parsing adjacency (cantools bit-level decoding, pfp 010-templates, laspy, borg chunker crypto) and should not displace the top tier. Downstream merge: prefer CalibForge security tasks; treat RTS CTF matches as strong-skill-but-unverified.
